recent_articles.title: Smart Border Project Is In Final Stage, Says Amit Shah
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** announced the rollout of **Smart Border** pilot projects across India's international frontiers to address evolving security challenges, including drone-based smuggling and human trafficking. The program will integrate district administrations, police authorities, and local institutions into a coordinated security mechanism.  Shah emphasized that lasting border security requires participation from all stakeholders and highlighted the government's commitment to strengthening infrastructure and modernizing fencing systems. He also stressed the importance of environmental protection as a mass movement and praised BSF personnel for their dedication in challenging conditions.

recent_articles.title: NDA And TIPRA Motha Signal Unity During Amit Shah's Tripura Visit

recent_articles.title: Kerala to Bengal, Why India’s Left Is Facing an Existential Crisis
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Communist Party of India (Marxist)**, once a dominant force in Indian politics, has lost significant power across several states.  This decline is attributed to the party's failure to adapt to the digital age and its inability to effectively engage with voters on social media platforms like WhatsApp. The BJP, meanwhile, has successfully leveraged these platforms for communication and mobilization, capturing public attention through nationalist narratives and coordinated online campaigns. This shift in political dynamics underscores a broader trend of the Left failing to address contemporary issues such as inequality and precarity, leaving it vulnerable to criticism and losing its ability to connect with ordinary citizens.

recent_articles.title: Mango The Sweet Diplomat, From Mughals To Modern India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Americans** are embracing **Kesar mangoes**, a popular Indian fruit, after a long-standing ban was lifted in 2006. This trend began with then President George Bush's appreciation for the fruit during a visit to India and has continued through subsequent years of diplomatic exchanges between the two countries.  The tradition of gifting mangoes dates back centuries, from Mughal emperors who used them as diplomatic tools to modern-day leaders like **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** who have received gifts of mangoes from other nations. The practice continues today with **President Pranab Mukherjee**, **Sheikh Hasina**, and others using mangoes as a symbol of goodwill between their countries.

recent_articles.title: Monsoon keeps India waiting, but brutal rain and hail to crash the party Monday - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** southwest monsoon is experiencing a slight delay in its official onset, but active weather systems are causing heavy rain, thundersqualls, and hailstorms across multiple states. recent_articles.title: BJP Core Group Meet At PM Modi's Residence Today, Rajya Sabha Polls On Agenda

recent_articles.title: TribuneIndia...AgricultureTribune

The decline in groundwater levels is also a contributing factor, leading to increased electricity consumption and farmer unrest. Haryana must implement artificial recharging methods like digging special wells along drains to capture surplus rainwater and replenish groundwater levels.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal AI adoption lag | Bengal and AI: For a ‘Deep State’ to aid technological innovation - Telegraph India

However, West Bengal lags behind, despite having a strong talent pool and intellectual tradition. The state's lack of AI adoption raises concerns about missed opportunities and potential stagnation.  This situation mirrors past hesitation towards technology in the 1980s, highlighting the need for a proactive approach to integrate AI into various sectors. A collaborative think tank, similar to the "Deep State" concept, is proposed to drive AI adoption in West Bengal by identifying high-impact use cases and fostering partnerships between government and private entities.

recent_articles.title: CPI(M), CPI: India's communists once ruled millions. What happened to them?

While the party has seen its influence diminish across various regions, it remains politically relevant in Kerala and continues to hold onto some support in other states like Tamil Nadu. The decline is attributed to factors including economic stagnation, changing political landscapes, and a shift towards identity politics. Despite these challenges, the CPI (M) insists on adapting to the modern economy and seeks to revitalize its presence within the Indian political landscape.

recent_articles.title: Amit Shah to visit border areas over next three weeks - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Manipur DGP moved to Cabinet Secretariat - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: West Bengal: Modi's BJP conquers one of India's toughest political frontiers

recent_articles.title: Why is India turning to crocodiles and snakes to ‘fence’ Bangladesh border? | Wildlife News | Al Jazeera

The BSF's directive to explore this option comes despite the fact that these animals are not native to the region and could pose a threat to local ecosystems and communities. Critics argue that deploying such measures is inhumane and ineffective, highlighting the government's use of fear tactics against undocumented migrants. This approach has been compared to similar controversial strategies employed in the United States, including proposals for using alligators or snakes to deter migrants.

recent_articles.title: ₹127.69 crore has been restored to victims of Rose Valley Group scam: ED - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Karbi Anglong lynching: Assam court convicts 20 for murder of Abhijeet and Nilotpal

The families of the victims expressed dissatisfaction with the verdict, stating they are considering legal options. This case highlights the dangers of misinformation spreading online, particularly through WhatsApp, which fueled suspicion and led to mob violence across India.  The incident also spurred a national conversation about how to curb the spread of false information and hold those responsible accountable.

recent_articles.title: Govt claims women winning unreserved panchayat seats in ‘significant numbers’ - The Hindu

The Ministry emphasized the increasing representation of women in PRIs, but acknowledged discrepancies between mandated and achieved quotas across various states.

recent_articles.title: Constitution Amendment Bill proposes possible change in size of State Assemblies - The Hindu

The Delimitation Commission, chaired by a former or sitting Supreme Court judge, will determine the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to each state and redraw parliamentary and Assembly constituencies. Public consultation on draft proposals will precede finalization before the new boundaries take effect for elections after the Commission's final orders are published in the Gazette of India.

He also criticized the BJP for hurling abuses against him and his party, stating they will win the upcoming election.

recent_articles.title: Tripura Government accommodating fake private universities, Opposition alleges - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **CPI(M)** and **Congress** members in the Tripura Assembly staged a walkout after bills were passed to establish three private universities.  **Sudip Roy Barman**, **Congress** leader, accused the government of engaging in suspicious financial corruption by allowing "bogus" institutions to operate. **Jitendra Chowdhury**, leader of the Opposition, alleged that the addresses and contact numbers provided by the applicants were not genuine, with one university's phone number belonging to a plywood factory. The bills are set to be introduced for another private university called "Dhanvantari University".

recent_articles.title: 33 detained Bangladeshi nationals sent back from Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nearly 33 Bangladeshi immigrants**, detained in Tamil Nadu's Salem district, were transported by train to West Bengal on March 20, 2026.  The operation was carried out with the assistance of the **Railway Protection Force (RPF)** and **Border Security Force (BSF)** personnel. The immigrants will be sent back to Bangladesh through the border after being handed over by the Tamil Nadu police. This follows an ongoing drive launched by the **Ministry of Home Affairs** a couple of years ago, aimed at deporting undocumented Bangladeshi nationals from various states.

recent_articles.title: ‘Family first’ in BJP list of bypoll candidates in Nagaland, Tripura - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** has chosen candidates for upcoming by-elections in Nagaland and Tripura, reflecting a dynastic trend.  Daochier Imchen will represent the Koridang seat in Nagaland, following his father's death, while Jahar Chakraborti is the BJP candidate from Dharmanagar, Tripura. The decisions follow the deaths of previous representatives in both constituencies. **Rashik Goswami**, a former BJP candidate for the Dharmanagar seat, and **Biswa Bandhu Sen**, who switched parties to join the BJP before winning the 2018 election, also died recently.  The party has announced candidates for by-elections in Goa, Karnataka, and Karnataka as well.
